title: General Lost Profits Analysis Versus Insured Business Interruption Loss Analysis
summary: Forensic accountants often perform similar analyses for lost profits and business interruption claims, but while lost profits analysis aims to measure total economic harm from wrongful conduct, business interruption analysis determines recoverable losses under specific insurance policy terms—often resulting in different damage amounts due to coverage limitations, waiting periods, and restoration period restrictions.
body_markdown: Forensic accountants, valuation professionals, economists, and damages experts are frequently engaged to quantify financial losses arising from business disruptions. While the analytical techniques used in general lost profits analyses and insured business interruption loss analyses often appear similar, the ultimate objectives, governing standards, and recoverable loss measurements can differ substantially.
